title: P-A/P-B provenance block shape drift -- source_frame_sha type, codebook_sha prefix

authority_basis.finding: §4.3 requires the 6 mandatory provenance fields (status/base_sha/created_at/created_before_p0_close/authoritative/real_target_outcome_used/requires_post_p0_reconciliation) and lists source_frame_sha/codebook_sha (among others) as 'record together where possible' -- it does NOT specify the shape or format of source_frame_sha/codebook_sha. This is unchanged from when the original CR-003 was raised (verified by re-reading, not from memory).

source_frame_sha.form: dict[str, str] mapping each input frame filename actually read by the lane to its 'sha256:'-prefixed content digest
source_frame_sha.rationale: must actually verify the content of the files the lane read -- a scalar copy of base_sha/input_authority_sha does not verify anything about input data content and is a semantic bug, not merely a format choice (see p_b_correction below)

grounds_for_selection: PHASE_GATES §4.3 leaves format open (verified above), so an anchor outside §4.3 itself was needed to pick one side rather than invent a third convention.

The current exec authority tip (bc0b7a0, V2-C012) already established a repo-wide sha256 identity convention in src/landing_accessibility/authority_manifest.py: compute_self_sha256() returns 'sha256:' + hexdigest, and sources/wiseapp/authority_manifest.json's raw_assets.*.sha256 entries are ALL 'sha256:'-prefixed per-file digests inside a dict keyed by asset name -- i.e. the exact same shape (dict of prefixed digests) this CR needed to choose between P-A's bare-hex-dict and P-B's prefixed-scalar. This is the most current, most authoritative precedent available in the repo for 'how do we write a sha256 identity string here', so both fields were normalized to match it.

P-A's dict-of-per-file-hash STRUCTURE for source_frame_sha is kept (not P-B's scalar) because it is the only one of the two that verifies anything -- P-A-QA (claude-b/pa-qa) independently recomputed all 6 of P-A's per-file hashes and confirmed exact match, which is only possible because the field actually stores per-file content hashes.

p_a_manifest.source_frame_sha: added 'sha256:' prefix to each of the 6 dict values (entity_alias_map.parquet, panel_registry.parquet, service_master.parquet, source_membership.parquet, source_ranking_rows.parquet, web_target_group.parquet) -- underlying hex digests unchanged, still verified against the actual file contents in this tree
p_a_manifest.note_added: provenance_schema_note field explaining the normalization and pointing to this file

p_b_manifest.codebook_sha: already 'sha256:'-prefixed -- no change needed, already canonical

source_frame_sha.before: scalar string 'd5f1da5652953542d5c8be377026cc3293f2075a' -- a verbatim copy of base_sha/input_authority_sha (a git commit SHA1), which per the original CR-003 finding does not verify any input frame content at all
source_frame_sha.after: dict[str,str] of the 3 files run_lane_b.py actually opens READ ONLY (verified by reading shadow/lane_b/scripts/run_lane_b.py lines ~127-133): state/service_master.parquet, state/web_target_group.parquet, sources/certification/certification_registry.parquet -- each mapped to its 'sha256:'-prefixed content digest computed against the files as they exist in this integration tree
source_frame_sha.cross_validation: the recomputed hashes for state/service_master.parquet and state/web_target_group.parquet are byte-identical to P-A's independently-recorded hashes for the same two files (sha256:86d665cc... and sha256:5262522d... respectively) -- both lanes are reading the exact same frame files, confirming no drift between P-A's and P-B's inputs
source_frame_sha.is_this_a_semantics_change: the underlying research conclusions (web_eligibility_status, mapping_status, etc. distributions in the manifest) are completely unchanged -- only the provenance metadata field's VALUE was corrected to actually mean what its name promises. The task authorization for this CR explicitly scoped 'metadata format only, not research semantics' -- this correction stays inside that scope because it does not touch any judgment, decision, or distribution, only a self-referential integrity field.
source_frame_sha.note_added: source_frame_sha_correction_note field explaining the correction and pointing to this file

p_c_provenance.reason: P-C's source_frame_sha/codebook_sha are typed str|None and left unset (None) -- this was not part of the original CR-003 conflict (that CR was specifically about P-A vs P-B disagreeing on a value both of them DO populate). P-C leaving them unset is compliant with PHASE_GATES §4.3's 'record together where possible' language (fixture_only=True lanes read no external frame/codebook, so there is nothing to hash). Advisory only: if P-C ever populates these fields in the future, it should follow the same dict[str,'sha256:'+hex] / scalar 'sha256:'+hex convention for consistency.

verification.self_consistency: after normalization, python3 hashlib re-check confirms every artifact_sha256 entry in SHADOW_MANIFEST.json still matches the actual file on disk (README.md hash also re-synced after its own text was edited for CR-001's count fix)
verification.pytest: no test asserts on the literal shape/prefix of source_frame_sha or codebook_sha in either manifest -- normalization did not break any existing test (confirmed via full tests/ + analysis/mapping/test_analysis_interface.py run, 316 passed)

not_in_scope: This CR does not adjudicate whether P-B's ORIGINAL scalar value was itself a defect worth flagging to P-B's own lane audit (the original CR-003 already flagged this as recommendation #1) -- this resolution corrects the integrated tree's copy in claude-b/integration-current only. The original agent/landing-pb-prework@9999857 branch is unmodified (per instructions, no direct write to Claude A-owned branches).
